convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in iMA indicators with simple EMA crossover logic, market orders, fixed lot sizing, and standard trailing stop. No custom indicators, no grid/martingale, no complex multi-currency logic. The Trade library includes are standard MT5 standard library helpers, not custom logic.

derived_values.name: Crossed signal
derived_values.formula: Crossed(SEma, LEma) when Reverse=true; returns 1 for up cross, 2 for down cross, 0 for no change

custom_logic_notes: The 'Reverse' input parameter (default=true) inverts the crossover direction: when Reverse=true, Crossed(SEma,LEma) is called so that SEma crossing above LEma returns 1 (buy signal) and SEma crossing below LEma returns 2 (sell signal). When Reverse=false, the arguments are swapped (Crossed(LEma,SEma)), flipping the signal direction. The Crossed() function uses static variables to track direction state and only returns non-zero on the tick where the crossover first occurs. Trailing stop logic only modifies stop loss on profitable positions; it does not close positions on signal reversal. The digit_adjust mechanism multiplies SL/TP/Trail values by 10 for 3/5-digit brokers to account for pipette pricing.
python_conversion_notes: Straightforward EMA crossover implementation. Use pandas EWM for EMA calculation. The Crossed() state machine can be replaced by comparing current and previous bar EMA values: buy when short_EMA crosses above long_EMA, sell when it crosses below. Trailing stop is standard: trail by fixed points once position is in profit by trail_amount points. SL/TP are set at order placement time. Only one position at a time (pos_total<1 check). The Reverse flag swaps signal direction - in Python, simply swap the comparison operators or negate the signal. Note the digit_adjust: in Python backtesting, work in price units directly rather than points to avoid the 3/5-digit broker adjustment.
